title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: Context (pp. 62-64): Grothendieck studies an exterior action, of Galois type, on the profinite fundamental group Pi_{0,3} of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}. This is the profinite free group on loops l_0, l_1, l_infinity with l_0 l_1 l_infinity = 1. The action is given by data g_0 in Pi_{0,3}, p in Zhat^* (playing the role of a cyclotomic character) and gamma in Zhat determined by them (formulas (11)). He asks when a 'presumptive' exterior homomorphism phi^: Pi_{0,3} -> S^+_{0,3} (formula (18)) commutes with these actions. Here S^+_{0,3} is the extension 1 -> Pi_{0,3} -> S^+_{0,3} -> S_3 -> 1, written Pi'_{0,3} on the next page. This is essentially the profinite completion of PSL_2(Z), with Pi_{0,3} corresponding to Gamma(2)/{+-1}. The previous page states the criterion: there exists beta in Zhat with (24), equivalently (27) or (28)-(29). On this page he rewrites the 'preceding formula' explicitly. The data are an element rho of order 3 lifting a 3-cycle of S_3, an element epsilon_0 (apparently phi^(l_0)) and an auxiliary element h_0. The formula reads rho^{-1} g^{-1} = int(g_0 epsilon_0^beta phi^(l_0^gamma rho^{-1}(h_0)))(rho^{-p}). He simplifies the argument of int to g_0 epsilon_0^{beta+gamma} phi^(rho^{-1}(h_0)). Taking inverses and substituting g, he obtains the boxed condition (30): h_0^{-1} l_1^gamma rho = int(epsilon_0^alpha phi^(rho^{-1}(h_0)))(rho^p), with alpha = beta + gamma. The g_0 visibly drops out of the box. The margin NB notes that existence of beta in Zhat satisfying (24) is equivalent to existence of alpha in Zhat satisfying (30). He then comments on a paradox. In (24) the exponent p does not appear explicitly, only h_0, while (30) depends on p mod 3, since rho^p = rho or rho^{-1} according to p ≡ 1 or 2 mod 3. In either form, he says, the condition seems clearly not always satisfied. As a programme he proposes to first make explicit the supplementary conditions of §39 in terms of (g_0, p). The next page turns to exterior automorphisms of Pi_{0,3} and of S^+_{0,3} via the exact sequence with S_3. Overall this is a step in his 'variations on the loop equation': deciding when a Galois-type action on Pi_{0,3} extends compatibly to the S_3-symmetric (PSL_2-type) group. This is the analogue of the 3-cycle (hexagon-type) relation in the Drinfeld-Ihara description of GT.
errors: The 'paradox' he notes (p appearing in (30) but not in (24)) is not an error. p presumably enters (24) implicitly through h_0 or the action data, so the equivalence is plausible. It cannot be checked fully without formulas (11), (18), (24).
The final assessment ('condition seems not always fulfilled') is stated heuristically, without proof or counterexample on this page.

ideas.what: Compatibility condition for a Galois-type exterior action on Pi_{0,3} to commute with an exterior homomorphism into the S_3-extension S^+_{0,3} (profinite PSL_2(Z)-type group), rewritten as an equation involving an order-3 element rho and its power rho^p
ideas.modern_name: 3-cycle (hexagon-type) relation for the action of GT / Gal(Qbar/Q) on the fundamental group of P^1 minus 3 points, extended to the S_3-quotient orbifold
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1990s), Lochak-Schneps; the orbifold M_{0,[3]} viewpoint by Nakamura, Schneps, others
ideas.where_published: Programmatic only: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) and La Longue Marche (1981) discuss the Teichmüller tower and Galois action; these explicit equations are unpublished

ideas.what: Observation that the condition depends on p mod 3 (rho^p = rho^{±1})
ideas.modern_name: Dependence of the action on the inertia of order 3 via the cyclotomic character mod 3 (the elliptic point of order 3 of PSL_2(Z))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in the treatment of Gal(Qbar/Q) acting on profinite PSL_2(Z) / SL_2(Z) (e.g., Nakamura, Lochak-Schneps)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets the task of making the supplementary conditions of §39 explicit in terms of (g_0, p), and suspects that the S_3-compatibility equation (30) is not automatically satisfied. This is an unfinished analysis of which Galois-type actions on Pi_{0,3} extend to the S_3 extension. It parallels the later discovery that the hexagon relation is an independent constraint in GT.
missed.quote: Pour bien faire, il faudrait d'abord expliciter les conditions supplémentaires du § 39 en fonction de g_0, p.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical interest: it shows Grothendieck independently isolating an order-3 constraint analogous to Drinfeld's hexagon relation. Mathematically this is now covered by GT theory, so little new content.

deep.surprise_reason: Technical intermediate computation in the loop-equation notes. The structure (an order-3 element relation depending on p mod 3) foreshadows the Drinfeld hexagon relation, but this is known to be implicit in Grothendieck's program and is fully treated in the GT literature.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 reads 'formule qui précède dans la formule présomptive (18)'.
Second display line is a simplification of the int-argument: g_0 epsilon_0^{beta+gamma} phi^(rho^{-1}(h_0)), presumably using phi^(l_0) = epsilon_0.
In the boxed (30), g_0 is crossed out inside int(...). The left side is h_0^{-1} l_1^gamma rho (repeated circled in the margin).
Margin NB: 'On a posé alpha = beta+gamma. L'existence de beta in Zhat vérifiant (24) équivaut à celle de alpha in Zhat vérifiant (30).'
'du fait que dans (24) l'exposant p n'intervient pas explicitement' — 'p.ex.' is an insertion above 'fait'.
The phrase 'Mais une fois établi... sous la forme du carré' is likely 'Mais que ce soit sous la forme (24) ou sous la forme (30)'.
The end of the paragraph is likely '...soit manifestement non toujours remplie !' (uncertain).
Last paragraph: 'Pour bien faire, il faudrait d'abord expliciter les conditions supplémentaires [?] du § 39 en fonction de g_0, p.'
